accepted.question_text: Classify closed 3-manifolds by defining model closed 3-manifolds such that no two models are homeomorphic and every closed 3-manifold is homeomorphic to one of them, without requiring an effective procedure to identify the matching model.

evidence.quote: We concentrate our attention on the classification problem of closed 3-manifolds

accepted.question_text: Can the classification problem for closed 3-manifolds be solved by cutting a closed 3-manifold along embedded surfaces, meaning surfaces without self-intersections?

evidence.quote: Can we solve the classification problem for n = 3, by cutting the closed 3-manifold along surfaces without self-intersections?

accepted.question_text: For a 3-manifold M with nonzero second homotopy group, so that M contains noncontractible singular 2-spheres, must there exist an embedded 2-sphere in M that is also noncontractible in M?

evidence.quote: does the family contain a surface without self-intersections?
Then there exists a 2-sphere S semi-linearly imbedded in M

accepted.question_text: Let M be an orientable 3-manifold whose fundamental group splits as a free product A * B. Must there be an embedded 2-sphere S in M such that M minus S has two components M' and M'', with fundamental groups isomorphic to A and B respectively?

evidence.quote: Then there exist a 2-sphere without singularities S in M

accepted.question_text: Is every nonempty proper open connected subset U of the 3-sphere aspherical exactly when every 2-sphere in U bounds a 3-cell contained in U?

evidence.quote: A nonempty proper open connected subset U of the S-sphere is aspherical
the sphere theorem implies Whitehead's conjecture (3.3)

accepted.question_text: Does Dehn's lemma extend from a Dehn disc with one boundary curve to Dehn discs with more than one boundary curve, while still producing embedded discs with the corresponding boundary data?

evidence.quote: There, is proved also an extension of the lemma, for Dehn discs with more than one boundary curve

accepted.question_text: Let M be a compact 3-manifold whose boundary is an orientable surface of genus h and whose relative fundamental group condition is pi_1(M,N)=1. Must M be a solid torus of genus h?

evidence.quote: Then M is a solid torus of genus h.

accepted.question_text: Is every simply connected compact 3-manifold whose boundary is a 2-sphere a 3-cell, equivalently, is every simply connected closed 3-manifold a 3-sphere?

evidence.quote: A simply connected closed 3-manifold is a 3-sphere.

accepted.question_text: For a knot K in the 3-sphere, if the fundamental group of the complement S3 minus K is free cyclic, must K be unknotted, meaning that K bounds an embedded 2-cell in S3?

evidence.quote: ifiri(Sz - K) is free cyclic, is K unknotted
this problem has an affirmative answer
